choices: To allocate memory for the object
To leave the object satisfying its invariant, so a badly-formed one cannot exist
To give the object a name
To set every field to a default
explanation: Fields default to 0, false or null, so without a constructor an object can exist satisfying nothing — and a half-initialized object is indistinguishable from a real one until it misbehaves. Validating here means the bad value never enters the system.
